title: bounded context node
description:
A linguistic boundary before a technical one: where the same word means different things, there are two contexts. It is itself a scope, so it declares no boundary and belongs to exactly one subdomain.

A relationship is named for every pair that integrates, and chosen deliberately. `separate-ways` is a real answer.

subdomain.description: The subdomain this context partitions. Exactly one; the classification lives on the subdomain rather than being copied here.

context_relationships.description: How this context relates to another. Authored edge, traversed only when expansion crosses a context.

x-alternation: Everything this kind requires, or a declared gap naming what is missing. A prohibition is not excused: a gap says a fact is absent and cannot make a forbidden field allowed.
x-open: `domain-object/1` types `context_relationships[].with` as `boundaryId`, which admits an aggregate. Only a context relates to a context, so the reference is narrowed to `contextId` here.
